30-second skim

Detect manipulation before the damage is obvious.

The project reframed market surveillance from retrospective investigation toward proactive risk detection across the full 2024 Russell 2000 dataset.

75%precision
77%recall
7,661high-risk events
GitHub ↗

The problem

Traditional surveillance often becomes useful after a sharp move has already happened. The question was whether anomalous behaviour could be surfaced early enough to help a compliance team prioritise intervention.

What I owned

  • Led a six-person research team and helped structure the analytical approach.
  • Built the anomaly-detection and continuous risk-scoring logic.
  • Connected model outputs to a Power BI surveillance workflow rather than stopping at model metrics.

Approach

Isolation Forest was used to identify unusual market behaviour across the full dataset, with forecasting/classification layers used to strengthen the risk signal. The final output translated statistical evidence into a 0–100 decision-oriented risk score.

What shipped

A ranked compliance view surfacing the most critical events, supported by a three-phase Manipulation Signature Curve and model evidence that could be inspected rather than treated as a black box.

Limitations & next step

The project demonstrates research viability, not a production regulatory system. A next iteration should test broader market regimes, strengthen explainability and evaluate false-positive cost under real surveillance workflows.

30-second skim

Turn job hunting into a data pipeline.

I built the tool because I had the problem myself: too many employer pages, inconsistent titles and repeated manual checking.

GitHub ↗

The problem

Irish job opportunities are distributed across employer career pages and platforms, with inconsistent metadata and weak ways to distinguish genuinely relevant roles from noise.

What I built

  • Direct collection from supported employer career pages.
  • Normalization of titles, dates, employment type and source metadata.
  • Candidate-match ranking and visa-sponsorship signals.
  • Saved / Applied states in the browser and a static GitHub Pages dashboard.

Why it matters

The interesting part is not scraping. It is converting an unstructured search process into an auditable prioritisation workflow that reduces repeated manual checking.

Trade-offs

Career sites change frequently, so connector diagnostics and graceful failure matter as much as ranking quality. The system is deliberately transparent about what sources are and are not working.

Next step

Improve employer coverage, calibrate ranking using application outcomes and add stronger deduplication across multiple sources for the same role.

30-second skim

Spot momentum before it turns into consensus.

EarlySignal combines fragmented market signals into a transparent opportunity score intended to support product and market discovery.

GitHub ↗

The problem

Trend tools often surface what is already popular. The more useful question is whether cross-platform and geographic movement can identify opportunities while they are still emerging.

Scoring logic

The First-Mover Opportunity Score combines velocity, cross-platform confidence, geographic diffusion, commercial opportunity and saturation headroom into one explainable ranking.

Validation

Walk-forward backtesting keeps the scoring process closer to a real point-in-time decision rather than evaluating trends with information that would only have been known later.

Product layer

A dashboard turns the model into a market-comparison workflow, while scheduled pipelines refresh the underlying intelligence instead of requiring manual analysis.

Limitations & next step

Signals are proxies, not proof of market demand. The next step is stronger outcome validation against actual product launches, sales evidence and richer platform coverage.
